speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The moon is new, if the almanac is to be believed, and the almanac has been right about the fast often enough that I will believe it about the sky. Sit. The loaf first. Then the price.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Short by a finger. A penny beside it. The stool did not rock when I set the board down, which is a new trick, and I am taking the credit unless the joiner wants it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The joiner may have the credit. I will have the breakfast. Threepence. A finger short. The moon can be new without the kitchen becoming a different country.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence, taken. And do not bring me a fish-sermon. The fast is Wednesday. Today is Saturday, and Saturday in this house is still a day a man may eat what the pot has. I am not salting the week ahead of the church.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Wednesday is Ash Wednesday. I heard ten days of it on Sunday, and the ten days are now shorter, and they are not today. I will eat what you give me. I will not announce a fast in a mouth full of bread.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The letter is gone. I looked for it by the cloak and the cloak was the only thing there. Is gone a good word this week? You used it about your father.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The letter is gone with Hobbins, which is what it was for. The cough is gone, which is what the sheet said. I am not reading the sheet again at breakfast to make the good news bigger. Just news. I have spent that phrase. I will not wear it out on a loaf.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Keep your phrases for the yard. I am glad the cough is gone, and I will not ask to see the paper. The rest of the sheet can live in your chamber. This table is a penny, a finger, and threepence.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then that is the table. I am not paying Edith at breakfast, and I am not paying a mercer in Cheapside from a lodging stool. Eight shillings and fifty shillings are still unpaid because they are still unpaid. A new moon does not settle them.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The wedge is on the shelf. I dusted round it. Three dirty leaves, very proud of themselves. Gib sat on Ovid and looked at the shelf as if paper were a rival, which it is.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Let the cat have his rivalry. Master Shakespeare, you play at two, and you reckon after, and you will come home without turning my kitchen into a counting-house. I had enough of a joiner on Thursday to last me a month.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: At two I am Egeon again. After that the sharers sit, and I do not know what the week comes to, and I am not going to guess it here to please a Saturday. Last week was thirty. Last week can stay last week.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Thirty what? Shillings, or lines? You have both kinds of numbers, and they are not friends.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thirty shillings was the share, last Saturday, the best since Christmas. Twenty-four is lines, and the lines are Kemp's, and they are not shillings. If anyone at the Keys tries to marry the two, I will not help the wedding.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. A married number is how a man pays the wrong bill with a cheerful face. Eat. The stool is level. The moon is new. Your wife has her letter. Your father has his breath. I cannot think of a fourth mercy without becoming Master Thwaite, and I have not got his glass.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Three mercies will do. I am not collecting a fourth. The horn is still the horn I bought on Monday, at twopence, and it has not become a quarrel again. We are almost a respectable house.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Almost. The spoon is clean enough to see. I would not swear to a sermon on it. I would swear it is a spoon again, and not a measure.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Swear to nothing before noon. Finish the bread. If you are reckoning this afternoon, reckon with men who keep a book. I keep a house. The difference is threepence, and the threepence is paid.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Paid. I will go when the bread is gone. I will not open the coffer before I go in order to have a brave number in my pocket. There is no number I am willing to say.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then say the moon is new, and go. A new moon is a thing even I can see is not a bill.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The moon is new. The loaf is short. The stool is level. I am going to be an old man for the third time this week, and then I am going to listen to other men not name a sum. That is a full Saturday from this side of the table.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: From this side it is a clean board and a cat who has won. Go. Come home when the reckoning has finished being pleased with itself. I shall be here, and I shall not have become Lent while you were out.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will keep Gib off the shelf. The wedge can be proud without a cat on it. If you come home with a number, say it plainly, and if you come home without one I will not invent it for the washing-up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: If I come home without one, that will be because there was not one to bring. Do not help me to a figure between the door and the stair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I never have, and I will not start on a new moon. Take the cloak. The loaf is finished. The fast is not today.
